data.title: Unconstrained Kerberos Delegation
data.summary: Hosts were trusted for unconstrained delegation, meaning they cache the Kerberos ticket-granting ticket of every user who authenticates to them. Compromising such a host yields the credentials of every account that has connected, up to and including Domain Admins.
data.description:
Unconstrained delegation allows a service to impersonate a user to any other service. To do so it stores the user's TGT in memory — not a service ticket, the full ticket — which is extractable by anyone with administrative access to that host.

A compromised host configured this way therefore becomes a credential trap. Worse, authentication can be coerced: an attacker can force a domain controller to authenticate to the host, capture its TGT, and use it to perform a replication attack against the domain.

This is legacy configuration. Constrained delegation and resource-based constrained delegation have been the correct answer for years, and unconstrained is found mainly on old application servers nobody revisits.
data.recommendation:
* Identify computers and accounts trusted for unconstrained delegation and migrate them to constrained or resource-based constrained delegation.
* Add sensitive accounts to the Protected Users group and mark them "sensitive and cannot be delegated".
* Treat any host with delegation rights as tier-0 and restrict administrative access to it accordingly.
* Monitor for coerced authentication from domain controllers.
data.short_recommendation: Replace unconstrained delegation with constrained delegation.
